items.titleEn: Micron stock hit by brutal 54% price-target cut: is buying the dip a mistake?
items.summaryEn: Buy MU. The selloff is driven by a target cut and a faster-than-expected return to DRAM/NAND balance. But the article shows earnings power is still exceptional (Q4 revenue and EPS far above last year) and AI server demand is still pulling forward memory needs (Dell AI backlog and AI-optimized server revenue). With MU already down ~47% from its June peak and trading at a low forward multiple on near-term guidance, the risk/reward favors buying while the market is extrapolating a future trough too aggressively. Key catalyst: share repurchases (up to $35.16B) starting 9 Dec can cushion downside if sentiment stays weak. Key Risk: Memory pricing doesn’t just normalize earlier—it collapses faster than expected, pushing MU earnings toward BNP’s 2029 trough sooner than the market models. Buy DELL as a second-order beneficiary. If hyperscalers delay some capacity plans in 2028, that hits memory demand later—but it also tends to shift spending toward “right-sized” AI infrastructure and upgrades, not full stops. Dell’s AI backlog and surge in AI-optimized server revenue suggest it’s capturing that spend even when customers become more selective. If MU’s cycle turns earlier, Dell’s backlog can still convert into revenue while memory pricing is temporarily pressured, creating a relative outperformance setup.

items.titleEn: SoftBank stock is crashing as Anthropic IPO signals a major warning for OpenAI
items.summaryEn: Sell SoftBank. The article shows a clear AI-valuation reset: SoftBank’s stock is at a multi-month low, long-term bond yields are ~10.73% (debt stress), and AI investment gains are collapsing (Vision Fund income down sharply). With the market already punishing Anthropic, investors will re-rate SoftBank’s OpenAI exposure lower and keep discounting future exits/IPO timing. Technicals confirm: below key support (~¥3,392), below moving averages, death cross, ADX ~35—bear trend likely to extend toward ~¥2,000. Key Risk: OpenAI’s IPO (or funding) goes smoothly and the market stops de-rating AI holdings, triggering a fast rebound in SoftBank’s valuation. Sell Arm. SoftBank is the biggest holder, and the article highlights Arm’s collapse (down ~65% from highs) tied to AI bubble fears. If AI multiples compress further, Arm’s growth narrative gets hit again, and SoftBank’s Arm stake becomes a double drag on sentiment and liquidity.

items.titleEn: Samsung, SK Hynix stocks tumble 10%: why smart money is heading for exits
items.summaryEn: Foreign investors are exiting Korea’s memory leaders despite record profits; Goldman and Morgan Stanley cut valuation targets hard, signaling the market is repricing the AI memory boom’s durability. The stock is down ~9% and the sell-side program-trading restriction shows broad, forced selling. Sell 005930.KS into weakness; expect further downside as DRAM price forecasts get worse (Goldman sees big DRAM declines into 2028). Key Risk: Memory prices stay firm longer than expected because AI demand outgrows new supply, forcing a fast earnings re-rate. Same driver, even more direct exposure: SK Hynix is the biggest foreign-selling magnet in the KOSPI (massive net outflows since early 2026). The market is treating this as an AI infrastructure de-risking, not a temporary dip—especially after Nvidia and global memory peers sold off sharply. Sell 000660.KS; downside is supported by industry oversupply fears and Goldman’s much lower 2028 profit outlook.

items.titleEn: Here's why the KOSPI is crashing 5% after Tuesday's historic rally
items.summaryEn: KOSPI reversal is being driven by a renewed semiconductor sell-off (Philadelphia semis -7.9%) and fresh memory-margin fears after Micron’s downgrade and oversupply risk. Samsung is the biggest index weight, so it will keep getting sold until memory pricing expectations stabilize. The stock already fell ~9% in one day—this is where momentum and margin compression fears usually extend for another session or two. Key Risk: Memory prices don’t roll over and AI server demand stays tight enough to keep margins elevated, forcing a fast rebound. Same catalyst, higher sensitivity: SK Hynix is most exposed to DRAM/NAND pricing and any oversupply narrative. With investors questioning whether 2027–2028 availability will crush exceptional margins, the market will likely keep repricing Hynix faster than the broader index. Expect continued foreign selling pressure and weak follow-through after the sharp Tuesday rebound.

items.titleEn: Why is Xiaomi stock skyrocketing despite a brutal earnings slump?
items.summaryEn: Buy Xiaomi. The stock is rallying on a real operating lever: average smartphone selling price jumped ~40% to a record 1,486 yuan and handset gross margin rose sequentially to 9.2% despite a profit collapse. This suggests Xiaomi is successfully passing through memory-chip cost pressure by shifting mix to premium models (e.g., Xiaomi 18 Pro), which should stabilize margins even if units fall. Add the support of aggressive buybacks (HK$13.1B in 2026 so far), which can cushion downside while margins normalize. Key Risk: Premium pricing fails—if Xiaomi can’t keep raising ASPs and handset gross margin slips back, the earnings slump reasserts itself and the stock gives back gains. Sell Samsung Electronics. The article highlights rising DRAM costs driven by AI data-center demand squeezing consumer electronics margins. Samsung is a key DRAM supplier, so it can look like a beneficiary, but the trade is about second-order risk: if DRAM prices stay high longer, smartphone makers (including Xiaomi) cut shipments and delay upgrades, which can reduce end-demand and eventually pressure volumes and margins for suppliers too. Short Samsung to express the view that the AI-driven memory boom turns into a demand slowdown for the broader electronics cycle.

items.titleEn: Billionaire Chase Coleman has been buying these 3 AI stocks
items.summaryEn: Buy Nvidia. Tiger Global added ~801k shares and NVDA is now its biggest disclosed holding. The setup is data-center AI spend plus a product cycle: Vera Rubin NVL72 starts shipping, which should let Nvidia sell more “full-stack” infrastructure per data center (including networking) even as clouds build some in-house chips. Key Risk: A major cloud customer shifts more workloads fully to its own accelerators and networking, cutting Nvidia’s share of spend. Buy Intel. Tiger Global increased its stake ~30% because Intel’s server/AI revenue is surging (+78% to $7.3B) while client/other is weak—exactly where AI agents need CPUs to coordinate steps. Add the foundry catalyst: first external customer for 18A-P. If early signings convert into real volume, both the turnaround and foundry narrative re-rate.

items.titleEn: Gold, silver extend losses as tech stocks slide, Fed inflation test looms - Kitco PM Report
items.summaryEn: (Kitco NewsWire) - Spot gold and silver prices were sharply lower in late U.S. trading Tuesday, reversing Monday's recovery as stronger-than-expected U.S. consumer confidence, renewed concerns about trade tariffs and another technology-led equity selloff pressured precious metals. Gold fell below $3,600.00 an ounce, approaching last week's 14-month low, while silver suffered heavier losses as weakness in industrial commodities and broader portfolio liquidation compounded the selling. Bullion failed to benefit from a softer U.S. dollar and slightly lower Treasury yields as investors reduced exposure to metals ahead of Wednesday's important U.S. inflation data. At approximately 4:50 p.m. EST, spot gold was trading near $3,552.50 an ounce, down $81.70, or 2.25%, while silver was trading near $40.790, down $2.250, or 5.22%, on the session. Gold traded as low as $3,546.00 during the day, while silver touched $40.570. Tuesday's U.S. economic data indicated a substantial improvement in consumer confidence and modestly stronger regional manufacturing activity, reinforcing expectations that underlying economic demand remains resilient despite elevated borrowing costs. The Conference Board's November consumer confidence index surged 11.4 points to 103.3 from an upwardly revised 91.9 in October , substantially exceeding expectations near 92.5 and reaching its highest level since January 2025. The present situation index increased to 132.8, while the expectations index rose to 83.6, reflecting improved assessments of business conditions and the labor market. The Richmond Fed's manufacturing index also strengthened to 3 from minus 2 in October, with new orders improving to 2 from minus 8 and employment rising to 6 from 3. Meanwhile, September house prices were unchanged on the month, while the national Case-Shiller index increased 2.1% from a year earlier, below the prevailing inflation rate. The combination of improving consumer sentiment, modest manufacturing expansion and subdued housing-price growth highlighted the uneven economic outlook, although the stronger confidence figures reduced immediate concerns about a sharp slowdown in consumer demand.

items.titleEn: Gold's selloff is sowing the seeds of its next rally – Theo's Iggy Ioppe
items.summaryEn: (Kitco News) - The gold market continues to struggle to attract consistent bullish momentum as expectations that the Federal Reserve will maintain its hawkish monetary policies into the new year have driven real yields and the U.S. dollar higher, increasing the opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset. However, Iggy Ioppe, Chief Investment Officer of Theo Network, a financial and tokenization platform, said that while gold has room to move lower in the near term, investors shouldn’t ignore the long-term, real-world value of holding the precious metal. He added that while most investors are familiar with the old commodity market cliché that “the cure for high commodity prices is high prices,” the opposite is also true, especially when it comes to gold.

items.titleEn: Huang tells staff that Nvidia does not need a succession plan
items.summaryEn: Buy a basket short NVDA exposure via relative value: short NVDA vs a peer basket like AMD (AMD) + Broadcom (AVGO) (long) and/or use an AI/semiconductor ETF long like SOXX while keeping NVDA as the underperformer. The news is company-specific governance/key-man risk; peers won’t face the same “founder too big to fire” narrative, so NVDA should lag on any governance-driven de-rating. Key Risk: A broader AI/semiconductor selloff overwhelms relative effects and drags peers down with NVDA. Sell NVDA. Huang publicly dismisses succession planning as “flawed,” despite filings warning that lack of succession planning can hurt execution. The stock already priced a “founder premium” rebound; now the market will demand a visible, investor-grade succession/oversight plan. Until the board names a credible internal successor/deputy or formalizes leadership depth, the key-person discount returns and multiple compresses.

items.titleEn: Michael Burry maintains Nvidia short thesis despite Jensen Huang's return
items.summaryEn: Buy Tencent (TCEHY / 0700.HK). Burry calls it a “Fortress business” and still undervalued despite AI spending. The second-order angle: if AI spend pressures near-term margins, the market discounts too hard; Tencent’s cash generation and platform moat should absorb the spend and stabilize earnings, making the valuation gap mean-revert. Key Risk: AI spending fails to translate into monetizable products and user growth, causing sustained margin compression and a prolonged earnings reset. Sell NVDA and/or stay short using bearish puts. Even with Jensen Huang back, the core thesis is governance risk plus accounting/antitrust overhang; the rally is leadership optics, not fundamentals. Burry’s own move—cutting puts after the spike but keeping the thesis alive—signals the downside case is still intact while uncertainty remains.
